title: Erdős 1180: representing residues as sums of modular inverses with small denominators
summary: A complete Lean 4 proof of Erdős problem 1180 and its quantitative variants on representing every residue modulo a prime p as a sum of at most C(ε) modular inverses n⁻¹ (mod p) with 1 ≤ n ≤ p^ε and gcd(n, p) = 1. Formalizing Glibichuk's 8-fold bilinear covering theorem via additive energy and Cauchy–Davenport together with an inductive asymmetric two-block prime-reciprocal construction, this development proves the affirmative existence theorem for all ε > 0 and all primes p, the discrete large-prime bound C_asymp(ε) ≤ 8(⌊1/ε⌋ + 1)² = (8 + o(1))ε⁻² (and ≤ 32ε⁻² uniformly on (0, 1]), the…
